summary_html: A child dies or suffers serious harm while **under agency supervision**, constituting systemic failure. Federal law mandates disclosure and review to identify causes and reforms.
authority_html:
- **Protect Our Kids Act (PL 112-275)** — federal commission and review requirements  
- **CAPTA §5106a(b)(2)(A)(x)** — mandates public disclosure of child-fatality cases

key_cases.case_name: DeShaney v. Winnebago County Department of Social Services
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that a child protection agency's failure to remove a child from an abusive parent, despite repeated reports and its own suspicions, did not deprive the child of liberty without due process, because the Due Process Clause imposes no affirmative duty on the State to protect against private violence absent a custodial relationship.
key_cases.relevance: The decision explains why a child death after repeated unheeded reports is generally not actionable in federal court unless the State had taken the child into its custody.
key_cases.quote: nothing in the language of the Due Process Clause itself requires the State to protect the life, liberty, and property of its citizens against invasion by private actors

key_cases.case_name: Union Leader Corp. v. N.H. Dep't of Safety
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the dismissal of a Right-to-Know suit for State Police records of the response to the Sununu Youth Services Center, clarifying that juvenile confidentiality under RSA 169-B:35 reaches records held by non-court agencies only to the extent disclosure would run counter to the purpose of rehabilitating delinquent minors, and remanded for that determination and for consideration of redaction.
key_cases.relevance: The decision opens agency records about incidents involving children in state custody to public scrutiny subject to redaction.
key_cases.quote: This refinement effectuates the juvenile delinquency statutes’ purpose of rehabilitating delinquent minors while also ensuring “the greatest possible public access to the actions, discussions and records of all public bodies.”
